claims.claim: An operating system is the system software that manages a computer's hardware resources and provides common services for application programs.
The operating system allocates the processor and memory among running programs, deciding when each program gets CPU time or space in memory.
The operating system acts as an intermediary between users/applications and the hardware, abstracting hardware details and providing services such as access to disk and network devices.

The kernel is the core of the operating system: it is among the first programs loaded at startup, stays resident in memory, controls all hardware resources via device drivers, and arbitrates conflicts between processes over those resources.

The kernel runs in a protected/privileged mode separate from user space, which protects kernel and application data from interfering with each other and provides protection between different applications and users.
Operating systems perform input/output control, resource scheduling, and data management functions.

A command-line interface (CLI) is text-only, driven by typed commands, while a graphical user interface (GUI) lets users interact visually with windows and pointers; the GUI proved more approachable for most users than the text-only CLI.

Linux is a Unix-like operating system created by Linus Torvalds that includes features such as true multitasking, virtual memory, shared libraries, and proper memory management, and has been ported to many hardware architectures.

As of July 2026, worldwide operating-system usage across all platforms was led by Android (about 41%), followed by Windows (about 28%) and iOS (about 20%), with macOS and Linux each a low single-digit share; Windows, macOS, and Linux are common on desktops and laptops while Android and iOS dominate phones.

conflictingEvidence.issue: How strictly to define 'the operating system' — kernel only, or kernel plus bundled utilities and interface.
positions: Some definitions treat the OS narrowly as the kernel (the always-resident core that controls hardware).
Common usage and several NIST definitions treat the OS as the broader collection of software that manages hardware and provides services, including the interface and system utilities.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson names the kernel as the core of the OS and treats the OS as the broader system software layer, which matches everyday usage and the NIST 'manages hardware resources and provides common services' definition.

sourceRecords.title: Operating System — Glossary
sourceRecords.notes: Authoritative anchor. Aggregates several federal definitions of 'operating system', including 'a collection of software that manages computer hardware resources and provides common services for computer programs' (SP 800-152) and 'an integrated collection of service routines for supervising the sequencing of programs... input/output control, resource scheduling, and data management' (SP 800-82r3). Supports the definition, resource-management, intermediary, and I/O claims. U.S. government work, public domain.
